correctness.rationale: The body has full diameter 2√(1+h²). In a 2-plane E the full-radius event is λmin≤c=1/(1+h²)≤λmax for the first 2-block Gram matrix. The oriented Gr(2,4) selfdual/antiselfdual spherical product has independent A=W12+W34 and B=W12−W34 uniform [-1,1]. The Rayleigh condition becomes ellipse x²/c+y²/(1−c)≤1 inside the diamond |x|+|y|≤1, with density 1/2, giving π√(c(1−c))/2=πh/[2(1+h²)]. AM–GM gives unique h=1 maximum π/4; Gr(1,4) event null and every Gr(3,4) has a deterministically exhibited witness. Independent finite Haar QR samples at h=.3,.7,1,2,6 agree to sampling accuracy.
residual_risks: Monte Carlo only checks normalizations and event implementation, not the continuous exact probability.
The proof uses standard SO(4)→SO(3)×SO(3) Haar factorization, which is essential and explicitly justified, not inferred from the sample.

originality.rationale: The exact πh/(2(1+h²)) two-disk-product diametral planar section probability is not a standard single-ellipsoid random-section result. The 4D Hodge product sphere representation and real Jacobi law are classical proof ingredients, not claimed novel. Inspected 2026 general random-diameter paper bounds diameters but does not give exact atom for this nonsmooth fixed 4D product; finite Grassmannian distribution and dimension trichotomy are new as far as searched.
